extracted.intended_audience: Reviewers for UAI 2020 (program committee / external reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for performing double-blind peer review of submissions to UAI 2020, including what to comment on, scoring rules, confidentiality/conflict rules, and procedures for discussion and rebuttal. Intended to help reviewers write efficient, effective, and well-justified reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: By viewing the papers, you agree that the UAI review process is confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, you agree not to use ideas and results from submitted papers in your work, research or grant proposals, unless and until that material appears in other publicly available formats such as a technical report or published work. You also agree not to distribute submitted papers or the ideas in them to anyone unless approved by the program chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double blind reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: The review process is double blind: authors do not know reviewers' identities and reviewers do not know the authors' identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPC members (area chairs) do know authors' and reviewers' identities. During the discussion period, reviewers see other reviewers' identities. Reviewers are encouraged not to actively attempt to discover author identities; if you suspect you discovered an author, first completely read the paper and then report the suspicion in the 'Confidential comments to PC members' box. Be aware that assumed authors may not be actual authors (multiple independent invention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: If you believe you may have a conflict of interest (for example, because you discovered an author's identity), you should contact your SPC member (area chair) immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accidental discovery of author identity occurs and a conflict is suspected, notify the area chair right away.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference system access / review submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviews must be entered electronically into the CMT system and can be revised before the reviewing deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may visit the site multiple times and revise reviews as necessary before the deadline. Ensure CMT emails are not caught by spam filters; if using Gmail consider adding a filter so CMT emails show up in Primary inbox.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Your responsibility as a reviewer is to read and judge the main paper; reading supplementary material is optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of space constraints in UAI papers, consider looking at supplementary material before concluding the authors did not provide a fully rigorous proof or only demonstrated qualitative results on a small number of examples. Some submissions include supplementary material in the PDF following references; others upload it separately—download separately if present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide structured review content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide written comments under the specified headings (Paper summary & broader context; Detailed Comments; Confidential Comments). Address both strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as precise as possible and avoid vague statements. Criticism should be constructive; when giving low scores explain actions authors could take to improve. If you think work is incremental, cite specific relevant prior work. If experiments are not realistic or useful, suggest improvements (e.g., more realistic datasets, larger datasets, different evaluation metrics, sensitivity analyses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary (Paper summary & broader context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain in your own words what problem the paper addresses and what it contributes to solving it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise summary that makes clear you understood the paper's goals and claimed contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the paper is a significant advance in the state of the art and its potential impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer questions such as: Is this paper likely to be read and cited? Does it address an important problem? What is the potential impact inside the UAI community and outside (natural or social sciences)? Does it raise new research issues? Is it likely to have lasting impact or be useful 5–10 years from now? Can other researchers build on it?

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the paper proposes genuinely new ideas or departs from the natural next step in a problem/application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty can be relative—assess in context of the problem/application. Reviewers should contextualize the work with past literature (inside and outside UAI), and may need to do a small literature search. Point out if the contribution is an adaptation or extension of existing ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Quality and Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether results are technically sound and whether claims are well-supported and reproducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask: Are there obvious flaws in approach? Is there a simpler approach that would work as well? Are claims supported by theory or experiments? Did the authors ignore relevant prior work? Are experiments well thought out and convincing? Are there obvious missing experiments? Will others be able to replicate the results? Are datasets and/or code publicly available? Is the evaluation appropriate and did authors discuss sensitivity to parameter settings? Assess both strengths and weaknesses of the approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess clarity, organization, use of examples and figures, and correctness of style/grammar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Is the paper clearly written and adequately informative? Are there problems with style, grammar, typos, formatting, references? It is authors' responsibility to write clearly—reviewers should not be expected to extract information from a poorly written paper. For poorly written papers, consider advising revision rather than acceptance; for likely-accepted papers, provide suggestions to improve clarity and list typos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements Necessary to Improve the Score
rubrics_metrics.description: List the highest-priority changes that would make you give a better score to the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize points; you do not need to comment on how difficult changes would be or whether they could be done for a camera-ready version. Include clarifying questions authors could answer in the rebuttal period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to SPC / program chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional section for comments intended only for SPC and program chairs (not authors or other reviewers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this box for remarks you do not wish authors to see—for example, rankings or comparisons among papers you reviewed for UAI, or suspected author identities/conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall numeric recommendation (6-point scoring system)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign one of six recommendation scores reflecting overall evaluation: Strong Reject, Reject, Weak Reject, Accept, Strong Accept, Award Candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scores defined in text: Strong Reject = Wrong or known results; Reject = Clearly below the acceptance threshold; Weak Reject = Borderline, tending to reject; Accept = Good paper; Strong Accept = Top 15% of accepted papers; Award Candidate = Top 5% of accepted papers. Use the full range of scores where appropriate; try to use 3's and 4's sparingly. New reviewers may calibrate using recent UAI proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer confidence score
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate your confidence in the evaluation on a 5-point scale from least to most confident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Levels: the reviewer's evaluation is an educated guess (least confident); reviewer fairly confident; reviewer confident but not absolutely certain; reviewer absolutely certain and very familiar with literature (most confident).

rubrics_metrics.name: Author feedback (rebuttal) handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Read author rebuttals carefully and consider whether they change your evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can submit feedback between specified dates; use the rebuttal response box to let authors know you read and absorbed their rebuttal and whether it swayed you. Keep an open mind—did you overlook something? Has the rebuttal changed your view?

rubrics_metrics.name: Area chair led discussion / reviewer consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: From discussion dates, area chairs will lead discussions to reach consensus on marginal or controversial papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in discussion to help decide borderline and controversial cases. Consider other reviewers' points of view—ask yourself whether their comments make sense and whether you should change your mind given the discussion.
